metadata.title: Implement WCAG AA & Screen Reader Support

story.iWant: I want to use the application effectively with assistive technologies like screen readers,
story.soThat: So that I can have an inclusive and equitable learning experience.
story.tasks: - [ ] **Ensure Interactive Element Accessibility (AC: 1)** - [ ] Review all UI components for appropriate semantic HTML usage (``, ``, etc.). - [ ] Implement `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, or `aria-labelledby` attributes for interactive elements where standard HTML is insufficient. - [ ] Verify and optimize keyboard navigation tab order throughout the application. - [ ] Conduct manual screen reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver) to confirm correct identification and labeling of interactive elements. - [ ] **Optimize Content Perceivability and Understandability (AC: 2)** - [ ] Ensure all text and interactive elements meet WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast ratios. - [ ] Provide descriptive `alt` text for all meaningful images and non-text content. - [ ] Structure content using correct heading levels, lists, and paragraphs for screen reader comprehension. - [ ] Perform automated accessibility scans (Lighthouse, axe-core) to identify and address content perceivability issues. - [ ] **Achieve WCAG 2.1 Level AA Compliance (AC: 3)** - [ ] Conduct a comprehensive accessibility audit against WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines. - [ ] Prioritize and implement fixes for all identified WCAG violations. - [ ] Generate an accessibility compliance report. - [ ] **Implement ARIA Live Regions for Asynchronous Updates (AC: 4)** - [ ] Identify all asynchronous actions (e.g., file uploads, content generation completions) that dynamically update the UI. - [ ] Implement `aria-live` regions to announce state changes and success/error messages to screen reader users for these actions. - [ ] Manually test ARIA live region announcements with screen readers to ensure correct and timely feedback. - [ ] **Testing & Quality Assurance** - [ ] Conduct comprehensive manual screen reader testing across critical user flows. - [ ] Integrate automated accessibility checks (Lighthouse, axe-core) into the CI/CD pipeline. - [ ] Conduct manual testing to verify keyboard navigability and focus management.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** any user-facing screen **When** navigated using a screen reader (e.g., NVDA, VoiceOver) **Then** all interactive elements are correctly identified and labeled. 2. **And** all content is perceivable and understandable. 3. **And** the application meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance. 4. **And** when an asynchronous action completes (e.g., a summary is generated), the system shall use ARIA live regions to announce the state change to screen reader users.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The system shall incorporate core accessibility features, including WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance, strong screen-reader support, and reduced-motion options.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The AI Study Buddy will adhere to WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance as a baseline. Beyond standard compliance, we will prioritize cognitive accessibility to support neurodivergent learners... Strong screen-reader support... Reduced-motion options.

doc.title: AI Study Buddy - High-Level Architecture
doc.snippet: The frontend is a single-page application built with React and Next.js, styled with Tailwind CSS.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: Ensure the application is intuitive, accessible, and enjoyable to use, fulfilling the promise of a clean, supportive, and frustration-free experience.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: As a user, I want the application to be fully functional and visually appealing on various screen sizes... So that I can access my study materials and tools from any device.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: As a user sensitive to motion, I want to minimize animations and transitions in the application, So that I can use the tool comfortably without discomfort.

code_artifact.reason: Defines the overall application structure, where global accessibility settings and semantic structure can be applied.
Implements interactive forms and elements that require proper labeling and keyboard navigability for screen readers.
Involves interactive elements, form submissions, and asynchronous updates, all of which need WCAG AA compliance and ARIA live regions.
Main UI elements and interactive components on the landing page require WCAG AA compliance and screen reader support.

constraints.constraint: All UI components developed must follow accessibility best practices, leveraging semantic HTML and ARIA attributes within the React component structure.
The application must achieve WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance.
Extensive manual screen reader testing (e.g., NVDA, VoiceOver), automated accessibility audits (e.g., Lighthouse, axe-core), and comprehensive keyboard navigation testing are crucial.
ARIA live regions must be implemented for asynchronous updates to announce state changes to screen reader users.

tests.standards: Unit testing is performed using Jest. Accessibility testing includes extensive manual screen reader testing (e.g., NVDA, VoiceOver), automated accessibility audits (e.g., Lighthouse, axe-core), and comprehensive keyboard navigation testing.

ideas.idea: Verify all interactive elements are correctly identified and labeled by screen readers (AC: 1).
Confirm all content is perceivable and understandable by screen readers (AC: 2).
Conduct a comprehensive accessibility audit against WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines (AC: 3).
Test ARIA live regions to ensure asynchronous updates are announced correctly to screen reader users (AC: 4).
Perform manual testing for keyboard navigability and focus management across all interactive elements.
